reconcile.note: Clarke argues the Genesis 3:8 language is accommodated speech for an infinite Spirit without bodily form, matching John's later claim that God is spirit.

discrepancy.note: Spinoza argues Mosaic law never taught a bodiless God and that Scripture itself implies Yahweh has a visible form.

quotes.text: the law of Moses, which might neither be added to nor curtailed... nowhere prescribed the belief that God is without body, or even without form or figure... Nevertheless, the Bible clearly implies that God has a form, and that Moses when he heard God speaking was permitted to behold it, or at least its hinder parts.
quotes.attr: Benedict de Spinoza (d. 1677), A Theologico-Political Treatise, Part I (1883 Eng. transl.), ch. I, on Genesis 3:8 and Exodus 24.

sides.snippet: They heard the voice of Yahweh God walking in the garden in the cool of the day, and the man and his wife hid themselves from the presence of Yahweh God among the trees of the garden.
sides.verseText: They heard the voice of Yahweh God walking in the garden in the cool of the day, and the man and his wife hid themselves from the presence of Yahweh God among the trees of the garden.

sides.snippet: a spirit doesn't have flesh and bones
sides.verseText: See my hands and my feet, that it is truly me. Touch me and see, for a spirit doesn't have flesh and bones, as you see that I have.\"
